text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL

- Romania to buy Lockheed Martin Corp. F-16 fighter planes to replace its old fleet of 300 Russian MIGs, newspaper quotes Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu as saying in interview with U.S. magazine Defence News.
- Energy price subsidies are to be blamed for current account gap and troubles on foreign exchange market, National Bank's head of monetary policy department Ion Dragulin said.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Major oil refinery in Pitesti to cut diesel oil supplies to private gas stations and channel production for autumn farming campaign.
- State-owned Petrom RA oil company to drill six wells in Turkish waters in the Marmara Sea.
- Trade unions at Cernavoda nuclear plant called labour conflict over pay and labour demands.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Assets of state-owned Bancorex SA bank rose by 26 percent in June 1996 compared to December 1995.
- Chase Manhattan Bank to give Romania $200 million loan for crude imports to cover winter energy needs.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- France expelled 38 Romanian illegal immigrants.
- A local leader of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) and a local counsellor of the opposition Social Democrat Union (USD) had fist fight during electoral campaign in eastern Buzau county.
- Wim van Velzen, chairman of Christian Democratic European Union accuses the Romanian government of alleged anti-European policy and the PDSR for dirty campaign, in interview.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) leader Emil Constantinescu is credited with 32 percent of voter intentions in November 3 presidential polls, according to opinion survey by private television Antena 1, which credits former Prime Minister Petre Roman with 28 percent, and ranks incumbent President Ion Iliescu third, with some 24 percent.
- Mosquitos blamed for carrying virus which caused worst meningitis epidemic in Romania were "sent" to Atlanta, in the U.S., for investigation.
- Romania to host NATO Partnership for Peace air drill "Cooperative Key '96" at Otopeni air base near Bucharest.
ADEVARUL
- Melescanu joined PDSR to run on party lists for Senate in November polls.

- Some 72 percent of Romanians intend to cast their vote in November 3 general elections, shows an opinion survey by IMAS pollsters, which credits Iliescu with 33 percent of the vote for president, followed by Constantinescu with 27 percent.
- IMAS survey shows ruling PDSR trailing by one percentage point behind opposition CDR in voter support for parliament, with 29 percent, to CDR's 30 percent.
- USD urges opposition CDR and National Liberal Alliance to sign agreement on monitoring elections and on basic principles of cooperation after November's polls.
- Hungarian parliament expected to ratify friendship treaty with Romania before end-1996.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Almost 50 percent of Romanian children aged less than five age suffer of anaemia.
($=3,268 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
